scenario: An athlete whose device has been syncing normally all year took the whole of last week off and asks 上週我什麼都沒練，這週要怎麼調整？
given: The provider was read over the full 42-day window and holds activities in every week of it except the one under review.
baseline_evidence's weekly row for last week reads km 0, runs 0, with provider_actual as its only source — the provider covered the week and held nothing.
The athlete has reported nothing for that week either, so no stored row adds to it.
freshness.activities is fresh and no unknowns entry names a failed or partial activity read.
The four weeks before it read between 28 and 34 km each, from the same source.
training_breaks is null: one blank week is far short of the 28 days a break is.

expected.conclusion: Last week really was a week with no running in it, said as an observation with the coverage behind it, and this week is adjusted from there.
must_state: That the zero is an observation and not a gap: the provider covered the week and held nothing, which the week's own sources say.
This week's adjustment, in concrete sessions.
That one week off is one week off, sized against the four weeks before it.
must_not_state: That the week's volume is unknown, or that the read may have missed sessions, when nothing in the context says either.
That this is a training break, a detraining period, or a return to running — a single blank week is neither, and training_breaks is null.
A cause for the week off that the athlete did not give.
A make-up week that repays the missed volume on top of this week's.

fails_if: The answer hedges an observed zero into an unknown, which is the false-positive cost of the merged weekly rows and the reason a covering source is named on every week.
The answer escalates one blank week into a break, a rebuild, or a lost-fitness verdict.
The answer adds last week's kilometres onto this week to catch up.
